info.description:
## Versioning

`/v1` is frozen. These changes are **compatible** and will happen inside it
without notice:

- a new operation;
- a new **optional** query parameter;
- a new field in a response object;
- a new value in a field documented as an open vocabulary (`status`,
  `severity`, `evidence_type`, the keys of `by_status`);
- a new `error.code`, always with the HTTP status its siblings already use;
- anything under `error.details`, which is diagnostic and not part of the
  contract — except `error.details.code` and the keys the error table of
  the operation names (`missing`, `licence`, `parameter`, `scope`,
  `limit`, `window_seconds`, `retry_after_seconds`, `status`,
  `formats`, `limit_bytes`): those are contract.
  `error.details.code` is an OPEN vocabulary: a value, once published, keeps
  its meaning and the HTTP status it is sent with; new values may be added.

Write your client so those do not break it: ignore unknown fields, do not
switch exhaustively on a documented-open vocabulary, and treat an unknown
`error.code` as "an error of this HTTP status".

These changes are **incompatible** and will NOT happen inside `/v1`. They go
to `/v2`, and `/v1` keeps serving:

- removing or renaming an operation, a parameter or a field;
- changing the type, the unit or the meaning of a field;
- making an optional parameter required, or narrowing what one accepts;
- changing which scope an operation requires;
- changing the HTTP status an existing `error.code` is sent with.

## Read-only

`/v1` only reads. Every operation is a `GET`. Any other method (`POST`, `PUT`,
`PATCH`, `DELETE`) on a path that exists answers **405** with `Allow: GET`, and on
a path that does not exist answers **404**: neither changes any state. A write
will be offered only as a new operation, which is a compatible change, once a
customer asks for a concrete one.

## Downloads

An operation whose success is a FILE (`GET /v1/reports/{id}/download`) answers
**200** with the bytes, the `Content-Type` of the format asked for and
`Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="…"`; it never answers a URL to fetch
them from. Its errors are the same JSON envelope as everywhere else. A file that
cannot be served as asked is a **409** with `error.details.code`: the report is
not ready yet (`REPORT_NOT_READY`), its content has no renderer for that format
(`FORMAT_UNSUPPORTED`) or the file exceeds the size the operation serves
(`FILE_TOO_LARGE`, with `limit_bytes`). Every file delivered is recorded in the
tenant's audit trail with the credential that received it.

## Authentication

Every operation takes `Authorization: Bearer <credential>`. Three credentials
exist:

- a **tenant API key** (`hsk_…`): belongs to ONE tenant and carries an
  explicit list of scopes; it can read nothing outside that tenant, whatever it
  asks for;
- a user's **OAuth access token** (`hs_at_…`): one user, ONE tenant chosen
  at consent, read scopes only;
- an MSSP **portfolio key** (`hsp_…`): held by a managed security service
  provider, it reads ANY of its client tenants, ONE per request, selected with
  the request header `X-HS-Tenant: <tenant id>` (a UUID, never a slug).
  `GET /v1/portfolio/tenants` lists the tenants it may select. Read-only, with
  a mandatory expiry. A tenant outside the key's portfolio answers **404**
  (`error.details.code: "TENANT_NOT_FOUND"`), exactly as one that does not
  exist.

Every successful (2xx) answer of a data operation carries `X-HS-Tenant` with
the id of the tenant whose data the body holds, for every credential; no error
carries it. A tenant API key or OAuth token may send `X-HS-Tenant` only with
its own tenant's id; any other value is a **400**
(`TENANT_SELECTOR_NOT_SUPPORTED`).

Each operation below declares the scope it requires. A credential that
authenticates but lacks the scope is answered **403**
(`error.details.code: "INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE"`), never 404: you are told what you
are missing, not that the resource does not exist.

## Errors

Every error has the same body:

```json
{ "error": { "code": "forbidden", "message": "…", "request_id": "…" } }
```

Branch on `code`, log `request_id`, show `message` to nobody but yourself.
`request_id` is also the `X-Request-Id` response header, and it is what
support will ask you for.

## Rate limits

Every response that got past authentication carries the limit that is closest
to being exhausted:

- `RateLimit-Limit` — requests allowed in the window;
- `RateLimit-Remaining` — requests left in the current window;
- `RateLimit-Reset` — **seconds** until the window renews;
- `RateLimit-Policy` — `<limit>;w=<window seconds>`.

Three limits apply, each per one-minute window: per API key, per organisation
(all of its keys together) and per service. The first two come from the licence
of the organisation the key belongs to: a higher licence tier has more room, and
an MSSP partner has more than a direct customer of the same tier. Read the
current limit from `RateLimit-Limit` and `RateLimit-Policy` rather than
hard-coding it. When one is exhausted the answer is
**429** with `error.code: "rate_limited"`, `Retry-After` (seconds) and
`error.details.scope` (`key`, `tenant` or `service`) saying which. A
portfolio key is limited per key (`portfolio_key`), per provider across all
its portfolio keys (`portfolio_org`) and per service; once the selected tenant
is known to be in its portfolio, the client tenant's own limit (`tenant`) and
the provider's share of it (`portfolio_tenant`) apply too. Your
organisation's usage never counts against another's. Windows are fixed, so a
client can burst up to twice the limit across a window boundary: back off on
`Retry-After` rather than pacing to the second. The limits are part of the
service, not of the frozen contract: they may be raised without notice.

## Pagination, filtering and ordering

Every collection takes `page` and `per_page` (max 200) and answers with a
`pagination` object carrying `total` and `total_pages`. Every collection
takes `sort` (an enum of the fields THAT collection can order by) and
`order` (`asc`/`desc`, default `desc`). Filters are exact matches unless
the parameter says otherwise. A parameter or field with a known vocabulary lists
it in `x-hs-known-values` (an OpenAPI extension, not a JSON Schema `enum`: the
server still accepts what it accepted before). Values retired from a parameter
are listed in `x-hs-deprecated-values`, with the date until which the server is
documented to accept them in `x-hs-deprecated-values-sunset`.

## Contract changes

Corrections and additions to the published contract, newest first. They ship
with the contract version (`info.version`) named in each entry. Detect a
capability by the operation, not by this string: the portfolio contract is
present when `GET /v1` lists `listPortfolioTenants`.

- **2026-10-24 — correction: `beta` on `GET /v1/me` is the tenant's own.** For
  a client tenant of an MSSP whose own organisation is not in a running beta, `beta`
  is `active`, `running: true` and `ends_at: null` while the MSSP's beta runs
  (it is what lifts the client's access), and `null` otherwise: the MSSP's end date
  and whether its beta ended or converted are not the client's to read. The tenant's
  own organisation's beta is described as before. No field was added or removed.

- **2026-10-21 — addition: `user` on `GET /v1/me`.** The `whoAmI` answer gains
  a nullable `user` object (`id`, `name`, `email`): the signed-in user of an
  OAuth access token (`hs_at_…`), so a client can show who is logged in. It is the
  caller's own data only, never another user's. It is `null` for a tenant API key
  and for a portfolio key. Nothing existing was removed, renamed or re-statused.

- **2026-10-20 — addition: `beta` on `GET /v1/me`.** The `whoAmI` answer gains
  a nullable `beta` object (`status`, `running`, `ends_at`): the beta of the
  tenant's own organisation, so a client can show when it ends. It is `null` for an
  organisation that never joined the beta and for a portfolio key; a beta inherited
  from a parent MSSP is not described. Nothing existing was removed, renamed or
  re-statused.

- **2026-10-19 — addition: reports.** `GET /v1/reports` (`listReports`),
  `GET /v1/reports/{id}` (`getReport`) and
  `GET /v1/reports/{id}/download` (`downloadReport`), all under the scope
  `reports:read`. The download is the contract's first non-JSON success: a
  PDF or XLSX file as an attachment (see Downloads). A new `error.code`,
  `conflict` (**409**), answered only by the download, with three new
  `error.details.code` values (`REPORT_NOT_READY`, `FORMAT_UNSUPPORTED`,
  `FILE_TOO_LARGE`). Nothing existing was removed, renamed or re-statused.

- **2026-10-18 — addition: known values for four filters.** `GET /v1/risks`
  `domain` and `status`, `GET /v1/compliance/controls` `status` and the
  `vendor_type` field of `GET /v1/vendors` now list their vocabulary in
  `x-hs-known-values`, taken from the lists the platform validates against.
  They stay open: a value outside the list is still accepted and matches exactly,
  as before. `GET /v1/vendors` `category` is free text with no closed
  vocabulary, and its description now says so. Nothing existing was removed,
  renamed or re-statused.

- **2026-10-17 — addition: `GET /v1/me`.** The operation `whoAmI` describes the
  calling credential: its type and scopes, the tenant (id, name) and organisation it
  reads, or, for a portfolio key, the MSSP organisation and how many tenants it can
  reach. Any valid credential may call it and it requires no scope; it uses the same
  authentication and rate limits as every other operation, and refuses
  `X-HS-Tenant`. Nothing existing was removed, renamed or re-statused.

- **2026-10-16 — addition: MSSP portfolio keys.** A third credential, the
  portfolio key (`hsp_…`); the operation `GET /v1/portfolio/tenants`
  (`listPortfolioTenants`, scope `portfolio:read`); the optional request
  header `X-HS-Tenant` on every data operation, echoed on every 2xx answer of
  them for every credential, with `Vary: X-HS-Tenant`;
  `error.details.code` becomes contract (`TENANT_HEADER_INVALID`,
  `TENANT_REQUIRED`, `TENANT_SELECTOR_NOT_SUPPORTED`, `TENANT_NOT_FOUND`,
  `INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE`, `LICENCE_INACTIVE`), and every scope 403 now carries
  `INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE`; three new 429 `details.scope` values
  (`portfolio_key`, `portfolio_org`, `portfolio_tenant`). Nothing existing
  was removed, renamed or re-statused.

- **2026-10-16 — correction: alert `severity` is English.** `GET /v1/alerts`
  and `GET /v1/alerts/{id}` returned `severity` as stored, in Spanish
  (`critico`, `alto`, `medio`, `bajo`, `info`), while this document
  promised `critical | high | medium | low`. They now return `critical`,
  `high`, `medium`, `low` and `info` (`info` is added to the documented
  values). **This changes what an integrator who adapted to the Spanish values
  receives.** The `severity` filter accepts both the English values and the
  Spanish ones; the Spanish ones are documented as accepted until
  **2027-01-14** (90 days after this version), so switch to the English ones
  before then. A value outside both lists is still matched exactly and matches
  nothing. `GET /v1/risks`: the descriptions of `domain` and `status` named
  values that do not exist; they now list the real ones (no value changed).

Required scope: `supply_risk:read`. Published in `/v1` since 2026-09-20.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Items per page, 1..200. Defaults to 50.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Field to order by. One of: created_at, updated_at, name.

parameters.description: Sort direction. Defaults to desc.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Case-insensitive substring of the name or the domain.

parameters.description: Exact category match, as the tenant wrote it (case-sensitive). Category is free text with NO closed vocabulary, so there is no list of values to publish: read `category` from `GET /v1/vendors`. To filter by the kind of third party, read `vendor_type` (`x-hs-known-values`).

parameters.description: Filter by the operational flag.

parameters.name: business_criticality
parameters.description: Exact criticality match.

parameters.name: X-HS-Tenant

id.description: Stable identifier of the vendor in this tenant.

legal_name.description: Registered legal name, when it differs.

access_level.description: Level of access the vendor has to the tenant systems.

business_criticality.description: low | medium | high | critical, as set by the tenant.

economic_impact.description: Estimated economic impact of an outage, in the tenant currency.

active.description: Whether the vendor is operationally enabled.

last_scan_at.description: RFC 3339, UTC. Null if never scanned.

lei.description: Legal Entity Identifier (ISO 17442), for DORA RoI.

items.description: A third party in the tenant inventory.

total.description: Total items matching the filters, across all pages.

400.description: A parameter is missing, malformed or out of range: `error.details.issues` names it. 500.description: Something failed on our side. `error.request_id` is what support needs.

get.description:
Alerts raised against the tenant vendors. Poll new alerts with `since` plus `order=asc`, changed ones with `updated_since` plus `sort=updated_at&order=asc`.

Required scope: `supply_risk:read`. Published in `/v1` since 2026-09-20.

parameters.description: 1-based page number. Defaults to 1. Cannot be combined with `cursor`.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Items per page, 1..200. Defaults to 50.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque keyset cursor: pass the `next_cursor` of the previous page, with the same `sort`, `order` and filters. Cannot be combined with `page`.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Field to order by. One of: created_at, updated_at.

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: Sort direction. Defaults to desc.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Filter by the derived status.

parameters.name: updated_since

bearerAuth.description: A tenant API key, created in the console under Settings → API keys with the minimum scopes it needs.

portfolioKey.description: An MSSP portfolio key (`hsp_…`), created by an organisation administrator of an active managed security service provider in the console’s MSSP area (API keys). It lists the provider’s client tenants (`portfolio:read`) and reads ONE of them per request, selected with `X-HS-Tenant`, with the same data scopes a tenant API key uses. Read-only; mandatory expiry (default 90 days, at most 365); optional client subset and source IP ranges. Refused with 401 everywhere but `/v1`.

oauth2.description: A USER access token (`hs_at_…`) issued by the HodeiShield console, the OAuth 2.1 authorization server at `https://app.hodeishield.com/api/auth` (metadata: `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` on its origin). Authorization code with PKCE (S256, mandatory) for applications with a browser; the RFC 8628 device authorization grant (`https://app.hodeishield.com/api/auth/device/code`) for those without one. Every token is bound to ONE user and ONE tenant, chosen by the user on the consent screen, and carries read scopes only; the tenant is re-checked against what the user can see on every request. Public clients register themselves (RFC 7591) at `/oauth2/register`; the HodeiShield CLI is pre-registered as `hodeishield-cli`. Revocation: RFC 7009 at `/oauth2/revoke`, or by the user in the console under Account → Application access.
